Question 1:

I understand that global effects aren't really global where you can choose the order in which the damage is received, that multiple effects with timing resolve in the order in which they were played (oldest resolves first) and that triggered effects begin resolving once the triggering conditions are satisfied but what about during the resolution of a global?

 

For example: Fanatic's holy nova deals each non-hero target 1 radiant damage. This one radiant damage kills one of gloomweaver's cultist. Do I resolve the entire holy nova effect first, or do I take a pause in the resolution to resolve the destroy effects then resume the resolution of holy nova?

 

Question 2:

Do "When this card is destroyed" effects resolve first before a "When a [card] is destroyed" effect?

posts.cooked:
Conditional triggers and effects:

Whenever you have consecutive effects being triggered that overlap, the newest trigger always resolves first. (This is not to be confused with simultanious effects. Those resolve in the order the cards were played. Ill get to that in a bit).

So for your first question, Holy Nova would be played and its effect triggered. Your first target is a Cultist and it gets destroyed. The Cultist has a triggered effect on its destruction, so you pause Holy Nova, resolve the new triggered effect by bringing out a Zombie, and now you continue to Holy Nova, including damaging that new Zombie!

Ok. Lets get into simultanious effects and triggers. This is your question #2.

"When this card is destroyed" and "When a card is destroyed" are simultanious triggers. They both go off at the same point in the cards destruction. I dissagree with Pydros assesment. For things like destruction and damage, there is a "before" period (this is denoted by "would be" triggers, like "would be delt damage" or "would be destroyed") and anything else is implied to be an "after" period (this would be why throat jab needs to result in HP loss before its effect can be applied). Because they are in fact simultanious triggers, Arenson9 is correct in that this will be based on the order the cards were played.

You can destroy something, have it stay in play while it resolves its "when this card is destroyed" effect, and then leave play. 

Where does it say that a card must leave play first before it is destroyed?

This is why the Sonic Mines question was ruled the way it was! Sonic Mines gets destroyed first. However, Sonic Mines has an effect that triggers when it gets destroyed. So Sonic Mines stays in play as it carries out its "on destruction" effect, but it is still tagged as "destroyed" and will move to the trash after its effect has resolved.

The Savage Mana + Sonic Mines is a good question. I would say they are both simultanious triggers and if Savage Mana was out first, Sonic Mines would not have the chance to do its damage. It is like killing a target with an End of Turn effect during the End of Turn. If it gets destroyed it does not still get to do its effect.

17. Can you redirect damage from Sonic Mine with Wrest the Mind?

Yes, as it is still in play to deal the damage before it exits.

This is pretty clear how Sonic Mines works.

The rulebook says "When a card is destroyed, it is removed from play...". You seem to be reading that as "A card is destroyed when it is removed from play" and thats just not what it says. Removal from play is an action steming from the fact that the card was in fact destroyed. Removal from play is not a pre-requisit in that sense, it is the consequence.

Edit: Also, just like one-shots moving to the trash when they are played, moving to the trash when destroyed is a baked in mechanic of the game system and not a card effect. Those do not follow the same resolution conventions, so order played does not apply here.

Thanks Spiff for the quick clarification.

Bunker with Ammo Drop destroying Tome of the Unknowable. Both of those cards have conditional triggers of a card being destroyed. These are now simultanious triggers, which means that the order of resolution will depend of what card was out first.

If this was Advanced mode, Tome would act first since it must have been in play before Ammo Drop. Its trigger resolves first, searching for Condemnatiom, then will move to the trash since it now has completed its final effect. Bunker now draws his card safely.

If it was the other way around, Bunker would draw his Ammo Drop card first, triggering Tome to play the top card of the deck (and newest consecutive triggers always go first). Fallen Angel would NOT heal the Tome, as the Tome has already been tagged for destruction. Then Tome would carry out its destruction effect, searching for the sword, and then move to the trash.

Now I know your next point already. But Kismet can get healed after being destroyed with Lady Luck in play, why not the Tome in the above example? Well, this is where Ronways proposed wording change matters. Lady Luck triggers on the same wording that Ronway proposes, which is "When X would be destroyed, instead do this" sort of deal. What that actually does is postpone taging a card for destruction and keeps them as eligable targets for other effects.

Now, I guess that Ronways proposed wording would makes the interaction much cleaner and less confusing, and if that change were to be made, I wouldn't hate it.

I would approach the second question differently:  Those are not simultaneous effects.

When a target hits 0hp and enters the destruction check, or when a dard is destroyed by a card effect (not HP) you enter the "unless otherwise stated" phase of the desrtuction check.

This is where Lady Luck, character cards flipping sides happen.

These are the "When a card would be destroyed" effects.

Next the card that is being destroyed must be dealt with, which includes its own text about when it is destroyed.  It is still in play, it resolves it's effect then leaves play.

As it leaves play all other effects that occur when a card is destroyed trigger.

Bunker would not trigger tome of the unknowable.  That would be wrong.  An action that occurs because a card is destroyed preventing that destruction would prevent itself.  Bunker can't draw a card because Tome wasn't destroyed.  But then Paradox.

I'd put the order:

1:  Destruction check is triggered.

2:  Is card indestructible, if so stop.

3.  Check for would be destroyed effects and resolve.

4.  Check destruction target card for destruction effects and resolve.

5.  Move card to trash, or other place if appropriate.

6.  Trigger remaining "when card is destroyed" effects.

I honestly think we overuse the order of cards played rule, it doesn't work well here.

This issue reminds me of damage timing, "would be" rext can take place before damage is certain, and before a destruction is certain, while "is dealt" takes place after damage or destruction is certain.  But even then there is timing differences.  Legacy can reduce damage when he is dealt damage, and AZ can turn damage dealt into healing, or respond to it with Isothermic.  That last example takes place after damage is dealt, not while it is being dealt.  It is a response trigger.  Bunker drawing a card is more AZ's Isothermic conductor timing than damage reduction reducing damage, it is a response trigger.
